name: LiteLLM

fit.headline: Provider breadth and a Python-first ecosystem.
fit.body: Evaluate its provider integrations and operational ecosystem. Review the documented Enterprise boundary for admin audit logs and SSO beyond five users.

choose_omniswitch: You want an inspectable self-hosted control layer in one Go binary.
Local guardrails, scoped gateway keys, and request traces meet your needs.
You can validate documented API subsets and accept public-beta boundaries.
choose_them: Your team already operates a Python-based AI infrastructure stack.
You need integrations from its broad provider ecosystem.
You have evaluated the relevant OSS, Rust beta, and Enterprise edition boundaries.

migration.headline: Pilot the client contract before changing traffic.
checklist: Inventory routes, key scopes, callbacks, and metadata.
Map routing, fallback, and budget settings explicitly.
Verify representative chat requests, streaming, tools, and errors.

name: Portkey

fit.headline: An OSS gateway with a wider platform path.
fit.body: Evaluate its routing and platform workflow. Check the current Enterprise boundary for SSO, SCIM, and audit logs rather than relying on older SaaS-only comparisons.

choose_omniswitch: You want to operate a compact self-hosted control plane.
You prefer local policy checks and a file-driven gateway configuration.
You will map provider credentials and keys explicitly rather than import platform config.
choose_them: Your existing gateway configuration or platform workflow fits.
You want to evaluate the wider OSS and managed platform together.
You have checked current edition terms for enterprise identity and audit features.

context.title: Portkey → Palo Alto Networks
context.text: Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition of Portkey on 29 May 2026. Review the current product editions and terms, not older SaaS-only comparisons.

migration.headline: Translate the configuration. Don’t assume it transfers.
checklist: Inventory configs, gateway keys, provider credentials, and policies.
Map retries, routing, budgets, and guardrails.
Verify request shaping, streaming, and error handling against your app.

name: Helicone

fit.headline: Your existing observability workflow still fits.
fit.body: Staying can be reasonable: services remain live in maintenance mode. Confirm roadmap and support expectations before committing to a new dependency.

choose_omniswitch: Self-hosted policy and gateway ownership are your primary requirements.
You can re-map your logging and observability contract.
You want a local gateway with an explicitly bounded beta scope.
choose_them: Your current observability workflow meets your needs.
You have evaluated the live service and maintenance commitment.
Avoiding a migration is more important than changing the gateway operating model.

context.title: Helicone → Mintlify
context.text: Helicone announced it was joining Mintlify on 3 March 2026. Services remain live in maintenance mode, with security updates, new models, and fixes continuing.

migration.headline: Keep the observability questions. Re-map the gateway contract.
checklist: Inventory routes, custom headers, and metadata.
Map keys, fallback behavior, and log fields.
Pilot representative calls and inspect traces before moving traffic.

name: Kong AI Gateway
column_note: OSS ai-proxy scope; AI license varies

fit.headline: AI governance inside your API platform.
fit.body: Evaluate Kong when its API platform is already part of your architecture. Advanced AI plugins have licensing boundaries; distinguish them from OSS ai-proxy capabilities.

choose_omniswitch: You want a dedicated self-hosted AI control layer rather than a wider API platform.
A Go binary and file-driven deployment fit your operating model.
You can work within the documented API and beta protocol scope.
choose_them: Kong is already part of your API platform.
You need to evaluate advanced AI traffic plugins in that platform.
You have reviewed the required AI license and Konnect operating model.

sources.label: AI Proxy Advanced licensing and scope

name: Cloudflare AI Gateway

fit.headline: A managed gateway at your existing edge.
fit.body: Evaluate it when you prefer a managed service and already use Cloudflare. Compare the network and control-plane model separately from a local self-hosted binary.

choose_omniswitch: Running the control plane in your infrastructure is a requirement.
Local policy checks and inspectable request data matter to your team.
You are prepared to own deployment and operations.
choose_them: A managed operating model is your preference.
You already use the Cloudflare ecosystem.
You have checked its current feature scope, logging, and spend controls.

name: Agent Router

fit.headline: Kubernetes and Envoy are already your foundation.
fit.body: Evaluate its Kubernetes/Envoy integration when that platform matches your operating model. Agent Router is the renamed Envoy AI Gateway, not the separate AgentGateway project.

choose_omniswitch: You want a compact control plane without adopting a Kubernetes-native gateway layer.
A binary, Docker, or a small self-hosted deployment meets your needs.
You value local policy and explicit protocol boundaries.
choose_them: Kubernetes and Envoy are already part of your architecture.
You want AI routing integrated with that gateway platform.
You have verified the current CRDs, charts, and protocol support for your workload.

context.title: Envoy AI Gateway → Agent Router
context.text: The project was renamed Agent Router in v1.2.0 on 6 October 2026. Existing API groups, CRDs, charts, images, and CLI names remain unchanged. It is not the separate AgentGateway project.
